overall: The AG found one violation: the Board's website notice for its November 29 meeting omitted two subdivision topics it then discussed and voted on. All other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Website version of the November 29 notice omitted two subdivision topics that appeared on the notice posted with the City Clerk.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board briefly discussed and voted on both the Carl Forester and Freemont Street Subdivisions during the November 29 meeting, we find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Open session minutes for the November 29 meeting were alleged to be inaccurate and to inadequately address the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: After reviewing the video recording of the Board's November 29 meeting, we find that the approved open session minutes provide an accurate and sufficiently detailed summary of the discussions that occurred.

allegations.summary: December 13 notice was alleged to lack detail because the 'Other Business' heading did not list the 22 Winter Street project specifically.
allegations.key_passage: Because certain information regarding the property was not provided to the Board until the day before the December 13 meeting, we find that the Chair could not have foreseen the need to discuss this topic when the meeting notice was created.

allegations.summary: Generalized allegations that the Board's notice posting practices and minutes generally lack sufficient detail were raised.
allegations.key_passage: We will not conduct broad audits of a public body and thus decline to review generalized allegations about notice posting practices or sufficiency of minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant objected to the notice statement that agenda items may be deleted or discussed in a different order.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not prohibit a public body from removing, postponing, or declining to discuss a topic listed on a meeting notice or agenda.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
